ut_cedar_city.blurb: Cedar City sits in southwest Utah, and its climbing is split between several kinds of rock within a short drive of town. Cedar Canyon holds limestone, mostly bolted lines, while crags west of town such as Pocket Rocks and Sprocket Rocks are on welded tuff and can be climbed all year. Swett Hills is the bouldering hub, and bouldering makes up more than half of the climbs, with a broad middle of V1 to V5 and a harder tail. Roped climbing is mostly sport, with the bulk between 5.9 and 5.12, plus a fair amount of trad and a small ice zone. The higher elevation keeps summer temperatures comfortable at some crags, while heavy snow shuts others in winter.

ca_san_diego_county_desert_area.blurb: This corner of San Diego County is nearly all about Culp Valley, a high-desert bouldering ground inside Anza-Borrego Desert State Park, on the road between Borrego Springs and Ranchita. Weathered granite stands on a sandy valley floor among sparse scrub, in tilted slabs and rounded boulders. Problems mix slabs, cracks and overhangs, running from beginner-friendly V0 up to about V10, with most of them in the easy-to-moderate range and a thinner hard end. A few top-rope, trad and sport lines are scattered around, with Glorietta Canyon and San Felipe Creek as small outliers. Late fall through early spring suits it best, since summer heat is intense, though the valley stays cooler than much of the park and the wind can pick up suddenly.

co_horsetooth_reservoir.blurb: Horsetooth Reservoir lies just west of Fort Collins at around 5,400 feet, ringed by public land. Bouldering is the main event, with Rotary Park the busiest and most popular zone, and the problems run from V0 to the low V10s with a big share of easy and moderate grades. Ropes come out for trad and top-rope lines at places like Duncan's Ridge and Torture Chamber, mostly between 5.6 and 5.11. Years of traffic have left the rock fairly clean. The sun is strong here, shining much of the year and punishing in summer, so cooler days are the comfortable ones, and the climbing can be done in any month.

pa_safe_harbor.blurb: Safe Harbor is a string of crags above the Susquehanna River in Lancaster County, spread along about six and a half miles of old railroad grade near a dam. It is almost entirely bolted, single-pitch sport climbing, with a modest amount of trad and top-rope. Grades run from about 5.7 to 5.12, and the heaviest concentration sits in the 5.8 to 5.11 range, with 5.10 the largest group. Most walls are a little less than vertical, with a few steeper lines, and the climbing is fingery face work on slick rock. Safe Harbor South is the easier-to-reach, moderate-heavy half, while Safe Harbor North has more routes, steeper walls, shadier belays and wider gaps between cliffs. The dark rock faces west-southwest and soaks up sun, so it is a cool-weather destination.

al_horse_pens_40.blurb: Horse Pens 40 is a dense boulder field on top of Chandler Mountain, near Steele in St. Clair County, in the foothills of the Appalachians. Everything here is bouldering, with grades from V0 to V11 and a wide spread through the moderates. The rock is sandstone carved by erosion into odd shapes, some looking like mushrooms or turtles, and it rewards slopers, tough mantles and committing top-outs. Some problems are tall enough to be risky. The boulders cluster in sectors such as Ten Pins Area and Deck Area/Front Slabs, set under a mature hardwood canopy. Fall, winter and early spring are best, when sloping holds feel stickiest, though bouldering is possible all year.

nm_white_rock.blurb: White Rock is a small community on the Rio Grande canyon rim just east of Los Alamos in northern New Mexico, at around 6,300 feet. The rim cliffs are basalt and offer a wide variety, from crack climbs to bolted sport. Trad makes up the largest share of routes, followed by a solid block of sport and a fair number of top-rope lines, with most grades between 5.8 and 5.12 and the middle at 5.10 to 5.11. The Overlook is the most popular crag; The Playground and Old New Place serve trad and top-rope climbers, and Below The Old New Place is a sport favorite. Style differs from crag to crag. Climbing continues year-round apart from winter storms, so seek sun in winter and shade in summer; July and August bring afternoon thunderstorms.
